reason: Uniform beta,M adaptive testing bound explicitly reported as Theorem 3; Gaussian testing asymptotics and eta definitions require primary body. Reproving reported theorem is ineligible; body unverified here.
statement:
In the Gaussian white-noise sequence model defined on page 35, let $0<\beta_1<\beta_2$ and $0<M_1<M_2<\infty$ be fixed, and let $D$ be arbitrary. For $\beta\in[\beta_1,\beta_2]$ and $M\in[M_1,M_2]$, define $\rho_{n,\beta,M}$ by
\[
\rho_{n,\beta,M}^{(4\beta+1)/(4\beta)}=n^{-1}M^{1/(4\beta)}\eta_\beta^{-1}\bigl((2\log\log n)^{1/2}+D\bigr).
\]
Does there exist a sequence of tests $(\phi_n)$, not depending on the unknown $(\beta,M)$ and satisfying $E_{n,0}\phi_n\le \alpha+o(1)$, such that
\[
\sup_{\beta\in[\beta_1,\beta_2],\,M\in[M_1,M_2]}
\Psi_n\bigl(\phi_n,\rho_{n,\beta,M},\beta,M\bigr)
\le (1-\alpha)\Phi(-D)+o(1)?
\]
The report answers yes in Theorem 3.
title: Sharp full adaptation to unknown smoothness and ellipsoid size

reason: All finite-measure open sets and dimension-only constant already reported as theorem on next page. Shape stability is a large analytic chain, not a finite certificate; primary body unverified.
statement:
For a fixed dimension $N$, there exists a constant $\c3=\c3(N)>0$ such that every open set $\a9\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ with finite measure satisfies

$$|\a9|^{2/N}\bbda(\a9)-|B|^{2/N}\bbda(B)\geq\c3\,\cal{A}(\a9)^2,$$

where $\bbda(\a9)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $\minus\Delta$ on $\a9$, $B$ is an $N$-dimensional ball with $|B|=|\a9|$, and

$$\cal{A}(\a9)=\inf\left\{\frac{|\a9\triangle\ B|}{|B|}: B\text{ is a ball with }|B|=|\a9|\right\}.$$

The report labels this assertion as a conjecture on page 25 and gives a theorem on page 26 asserting that it holds for every such open set.
title: Quantitative Faber–Krahn inequality with Fraenkel asymmetry

reason: All Gaussian channels, all states and concave f, including uniqueness under strict hypotheses, require operator majorization and precise channel definitions. No full mechanism or body clearance.
statement:
Let \(\Phi\) be a gauge-covariant or gauge-contravariant Bosonic Gaussian channel, as defined by equations (2)–(5) on PDF pages 29–30, and let \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave with \(f(0)=0\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Tr} f(\Phi[\rho])\geq \operatorname{Tr}f\bigl(\Phi[|w\rangle\langle w|]\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}f\bigl(\Phi[|0\rangle\langle0|]\bigr)
\]
for every state \(\rho\) and every coherent state \(|w\rangle\langle w|\). If, in addition, \(f\) is strictly concave, \(KK^*>0\), and the relevant inequalities (3) and (5) hold strictly, equality occurs only when \(\rho\) is a coherent state.
title: Quantum Gaussian optimizers for gauge-covariant and contravariant channels

reason: Every admissible Hamiltonian,b,gamma requires Nevanlinna representation and transfer-matrix positivity; class N and endpoint hypotheses are source dependent. No new full route.
statement:
Consider the canonical system $-Jy'(x)=zH(x)y(x)$ on $[0,\ell)$ with $y_2(0)=0$, where $H$ is a real symmetric non-negative measurable $2\times2$ matrix, $\operatorname{tr}H(x)=1$ almost everywhere, and $\int_0^\varepsilon h_{22}(x)\,dx>0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Let $W(x;z)=(w_{ij}(x;z))_{i,j=1}^2$ solve $\frac{dW(x;z)}{dx}J=zW(x;z)H(x)$, $W(0;z)=I_2$. If $0<b\leq\ell$, $b<\infty$, and $\gamma\in\widetilde{N}:=N\cup\{\infty\}$, then
$$m_\gamma(z):=\frac{w_{11}(b;z)\gamma(z)+w_{12}(b;z)}{w_{21}(b;z)\gamma(z)+w_{22}(b;z)}$$
belongs to the class $N$ and has the representation
$$m_\gamma(z)=\alpha+\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-z}-\frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda^2}\right)d\tau_\gamma(\lambda),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R},$$
for some $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$.
title: Spectral-measure parametrization for a canonical system

reason: Conditional on BG inequality; constructing virtual DT counts for every rational cohomology class requires stability and moduli machinery. A parameter computation cannot establish the asserted map.
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi–Yau $3$-fold satisfying Conjecture 1 (the BG-type inequality stated on PDF page 11). Then, for every $v\in H^*(X,\mathbb{Q})$, there is a map
\[
\mathrm{DT}^*(v):\operatorname{Stab}^{\circ}_{\omega,B}(X)\longrightarrow \mathbb{Q}
\]
such that $\mathrm{DT}_{\sigma}(v)$ virtually counts $\sigma$-semistable objects $E\in D^b\operatorname{Coh}(X)$ with $\operatorname{ch}(E)=v$.
title: Donaldson–Thomas invariants for Bridgeland-semistable objects on Calabi–Yau 3-folds

reason: All g,k explicit stretch-factor bounds are attributed to named authors. Requires geometric lower bound plus uniform construction; no short full route or inspected proof body.
statement:
Let $S_g$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g\ge 2$. For a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism $f:S_g\to S_g$, let $\kappa(f)=\dim\operatorname{Fix}(f_*)$, where $f_*$ is the induced action on $H_1(S_g;\mathbb R)$. Define
\[
\ell_g(k)=\min\{\log(\lambda(f))\mid f:S_g\to S_g\text{ is pseudo-Anosov and }\kappa(f)\ge k\}.
\]
Then, for all $g\ge 2$ and $0\le k\le 2g$,
\[
0.00031\,\frac{k+1}{2g-2}\le \ell_g(k)\le 12\log(2)\,\frac{k+1}{2g-2}.
\]
Equivalently, $\ell_g(k)\asymp (k+1)/g$.
title: Agol–Leininger–Margalit bounds for pseudo-Anosov stretch factors and homology

reason: Explicit polynomial-time extractor for every independent source pair with logarithmic entropy requires uniform pseudorandom construction and error analysis; stated C=75 is not novelty evidence.
statement: There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a polynomial-time computable function $2\mathrm{Ext}:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ such that, for every pair of independent $(n,k)$-sources $X,Y$ with $k\ge \log^C(n)$, the output $2\mathrm{Ext}(X,Y)$ is within statistical distance $n^{-\Omega(1)}$ of the uniform distribution on one bit. The report states that $C=75$ suffices.
title: Explicit two-source extractors for polylogarithmic min-entropy

reason: Finite d=2..10 does not make arbitrary-field incidence realizability finite automatically. Need classification and realizable extremizers over all characteristics, not only combinatorial incidence counts.
statement:
Let $K$ be an arbitrary field, and let $\mathcal L=\{L_1,\ldots,L_d\}$ be a configuration of $d$ mutually distinct lines in $\mathbb P^2(K)$. If $\mathcal P(\mathcal L)=\{P_1,\ldots,P_s\}$ is the set of singular points and $m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)$ is the number of lines through $P_k$, define
\[
H_L(K,\mathcal L)=\frac{d^2-\sum_{k=1}^s m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)^2}{s},\qquad H_L(K,d)=\min_{\mathcal L}H_L(K,\mathcal L),
\]
and
\[
H_L(d)=\min_K H_L(K,d).
\]
The absolute linear Harbourne constants for $2\le d\le 10$ are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
d&2&3&4&5&6&7&8&9&10\\ \hline
H_L(d)&0&-1&-\frac43&-\frac32&-\frac{12}{7}&-2&-2&-\frac94&-\frac{29}{12}
\end{array}
\]
title: Absolute linear Harbourne constants for at most ten lines

reason: Existence for each of 59 unspecified lattices and some rescaling requires automorphic construction, integral coefficients and multiplicity-one divisor. Missing explicit lattice list and no full certificate route.
statement: **Conjecture.** For all 59 lattices $S$ of Theorem 3, there exists some $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for $T=U(m)\oplus S$ of signature $(n+1,2)$, there is a 2-reflective holomorphic automorphic form $\Phi(z)\in M_k(\Gamma)$ of weight $k>0$ with integral Fourier coefficients, where $\Gamma\subset O(T)$ is of finite index, and whose divisor is the union of rational quadratic divisors, with multiplicity one, orthogonal to the elements of $T$ having square $2$.
title: Existence of 2-reflective automorphic forms for the 59 lattices

reason: Matching tower-height upper and lower bounds as epsilon tends to zero need global additive-combinatorial constructions. A finite-field parameter example cannot settle the asymptotics.
statement: For a prime $p$, let $n_p(\varepsilon)$ be the least positive integer such that, for every $n\ge n_p(\varepsilon)$ and every subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^n$ of density $\alpha$, there is a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p^n$ such that the density of three-term arithmetic progressions with common difference $d$ that are in $A$ is at least $\alpha^3-\varepsilon$. For $\varepsilon<2^{-500}p^{-8}$, $n_p(\varepsilon)$ grows as an exponential tower of $p$’s of height $\Theta(\log(1/\varepsilon))$.
title: Tower-type bound for Green’s popular progression-differences theorem

reason: Condition (11), gamma, spaces and small-state norm depend on primary definitions. Uniform local growth in every admissible control requires analytic second-variation estimates; no finite shortcut.
statement:
Under the first-order optimality conditions, condition (11), and the additional hypothesis
\[
\exists K>0\ \forall\varepsilon>0:\ \left|\left\{t\in(0,T):\left|\int_{\Omega}\bar\varphi(t)g_j\,dx\right|<\varepsilon\right\}\right|\le K\varepsilon\quad\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,m\},
\]
there exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\nu>0\), and \(\kappa>0\) such that
\[
J(\bar u)+\frac{\nu}{2}\|u-\bar u\|_{L^1(Q)}^{1+1/\gamma}+\frac{\kappa}{2}\|y_u-\bar y\|_{L^2(Q)}^2\le J(u)
\]
for every \(u\in U_{ad}\) satisfying \(\|y_u-\bar y\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}<\varepsilon\).
title: Second-order growth and control error estimates for a bang-bang parabolic control problem

reason: All n>=6 resolvent-degree lower bounds require embeddings and essential-rank definitions plus geometric obstruction. Checking finitely many ranks is not full scope.
statement:
For every integer $n\ge 6$, Conjecture 12 asserts
\[
\operatorname{RD}\!\left(\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{g,2}\to \mathcal A_g^{A_n}\right)\ge e_{A_n},
\]
where $A_n\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb F_2)$ is the embedding from Proposition 11, $\mathcal A_g^{A_n}=\widetilde{\mathcal A}_{g,2}/A_n$, and $e_{A_n}=\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb F_2}(A_n\cap U)$ for the unipotent radical $U$ of the Siegel parabolic.
title: Resolvent-degree lower bound for alternating-group quotients of the level-2 abelian-variety cover

reason: All eccentricities in a punctured interval require validated dynamical estimates uniform in epsilon. Tiny explicit constants do not supply a small exact orbit certificate or diffusion proof.
statement:
For the planar elliptic restricted three-body problem with the Neptune–Triton parameters, namely normalized mass ratio $\mu=0.0002089$ and primary eccentricity bound $\varepsilon_1=1.6\times 10^{-5}$, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,\varepsilon_1]$ there exist a point $z(\varepsilon)$ and a time $t(\varepsilon)\in(0,T/\varepsilon)$ such that
$$
H_0\!\left(\Phi^{\varepsilon}_{t(\varepsilon)}(z(\varepsilon))\right)-H_0\!\left(z(\varepsilon)\right)>C,
$$
where $C=2\times10^{-9}$ and $T=5.7\times10^{-4}$; here $H_0$ is the circular problem’s Hamiltonian and $\Phi_t^\varepsilon$ is the flow of the elliptic problem.
title: Existence of energy-diffusing orbits in the planar elliptic restricted three-body problem

reason: All rational elliptic-curve congruences for every prime>=17 require global exclusion outside two twist families; finite conductor or prime scans cannot certify completeness.
statement: For every prime $p\ge 17$, the only non-trivial pairs of $p$-congruent elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ are the two examples described in the report—one symplectic pair, with conductors $279809270$ and $3077901970$, and one anti-symplectic pair, with conductors $3675$ and $47775$—together with their simultaneous quadratic twists. Here, a non-trivial congruence is one not arising from an isogeny of degree coprime to $p$.
title: Fisher’s conjecture on non-trivial prime-level congruences for primes at least 17

reason: For each k and sufficiently large n exact density inequality needs asymptotic extremal argument or scalable violating construction. No full-family mechanism identified; no brute force invested.
statement:
**Conjecture 4.** Fix $k\ge 2$. For all sufficiently large $n$ (depending on $k$), every $n$-vertex partially directed $k$-uniform hypergraph ($k$-PDG) without $\vec T_k$ as a subgraph satisfies
\[
\alpha+(\log_2 3)\beta\le 1,
\]
where $\alpha$ is the number of undirected edges divided by $\binom{n}{k}$ and $\beta$ is the number of directed edges divided by $\binom{n}{k}$. Here a $k$-PDG is obtained by orienting some edges of a $k$-uniform hypergraph, with an oriented edge recording a selected vertex; subgraphs may be formed by deleting vertices, edges, and orientations. The forbidden $k$-PDG $\vec T_k$ is obtained from $\vec T_2$, whose edges are $12$, the directed edge $1\to 3$, and $23$, by adding $k-2$ common vertices to all three edges.
title: Turán inequality for partially directed uniform hypergraphs

reason: All nonfaithful cyclic actions require primitive rational central idempotents and integral nilpotent witnesses. Even C17 semidirect C8 requires action-specific Wedderburn data. No full-scope or exact obstruction justified.
statement: We say that a finite group $G$ has the nilpotent decomposition property if, for every nilpotent element $n\in \mathbb{Z}G$ in the integral group ring of $G$ and every primitive central idempotent $e\in\mathbb{Q}G$ in the rational group algebra of $G$, the product $ne$ lies in $\mathbb{Z}G$. Does this property hold for groups of shape $C_p\rtimes C_{q^k}$, where $p$ and $q$ are primes, $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and the action of $C_{q^k}$ is not faithful? In particular, consider $C_{17}\rtimes C_8$ with the action by inversion.
title: Nilpotent decomposition property for nonfaithful cyclic semidirect products

statement:
For every positive integer \(d\), the genus-1 invariant satisfies
\[
\left\langle D\right\rangle^{\operatorname{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{C}^2)}_1
= -\frac{1}{24}\frac{(t_1+t_2)^2}{t_1t_2}
\left(\operatorname{Tr}_d+\sum_{e=1}^{d-1}\sigma_{-1}(d-e)\operatorname{Tr}_e\right),
\]
where \(\operatorname{Tr}_e\) is the trace of quantum multiplication by the divisor \(D\), and \(\sigma_{-1}(m)=\sum_{r\mid m}r^{-1}\).
title: Closed expression for the genus-1 divisor invariant of \(\operatorname{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{C}^2)\)

statement: Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$? More precisely: does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ and all nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density $\alpha > 0$, the sumset $10A$ contains a coset of some subspace of dimension at least $n - C \log_2(1/\alpha)$? The sumset $10A$ is defined as $\{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10} : a_i \in A\}$, using the pointwise scalar multiplication notation `10 • A` where `•` denotes the iterated addition of a set. Note: We model $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as `Fin n → ZMod 2`, which is an $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
title: Green problem 50

title: Bicriteria submodular maximization over $p$-systems

reason: Every multiple of four requires unrestricted Hadamard construction; Sylvester orders and isolated examples leave full scope untouched.
statement:
For a positive integer $n$, call a matrix $H$ a *Hadamard matrix of order $n$*
if

$$
H\in\{-1,1\}^{n\times n},\qquad HH^{\mathsf{T}}=n\,I_{n},
$$

where $I_{n}$ is the $n\times n$ identity matrix and $H^{\mathsf{T}}$ is the
transpose of $H$; equivalently, the rows of $H$ are pairwise orthogonal vectors
in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$, so that any two distinct rows of $H$ agree in exactly
$n/2$ of the $n$ coordinates, and $|\det H|=n^{n/2}$.

For every positive integer $k$ there exists a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$.
title: Hadamard conjecture

reason: Williamson universal existence has a known-counterexample warning, but no original nonexistence proof body inspected here. Do not generate or credit another classical finite instance; primary publication required.
statement:
For a positive integer $n$, call a matrix $M=(m_{i,j})_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ with
entries $m_{i,j}\in\{+1,-1\}$ circulant if $m_{i,j}$ depends only on
$j-i \bmod n$, i.e. there is a sequence
$(a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1})\in\{+1,-1\}^n$ with $m_{i,j}=a_{(j-i)\bmod
n}$ for all $i,j$, and symmetric if $M^{\mathsf T}=M$. Four matrices
$A,B,C,D$ of order $n$ are Williamson matrices of order
$n$ if each of them has all entries in $\{+1,-1\}$, each is symmetric and
circulant, and

$$
A^{2}+B^{2}+C^{2}+D^{2}=4n\,I_{n},
$$

where $I_{n}$ is the identity matrix of order $n$.

For every positive integer $n$, there exist Williamson matrices of order $n$.
title: Williamson conjecture

reason: Arbitrary nonunital associative rings and sums of nil left ideals require ring-theoretic global mechanism. Elementwise nilpotence has no uniform exponent; finite rings do not resolve it.
statement:
Let
$R$ be an associative ring, not necessarily commutative and not necessarily possessing a multiplicative identity. An element $a
\in R$ is nilpotent if $a^{n} = 0$ for some integer $n \ge
1$, and a subset of $R$ is called nil if each of its elements is nilpotent.
Then:

If the only nil two-sided ideal of $R$ is $\{0\}$, then the only nil one-sided
(left or right) ideal of $R$ is $\{0\}$.

Equivalently, for every associative ring $R$ and all nil left ideals $I, J
\subseteq R$, the left ideal $I + J$ is nil.
title: Köthe conjecture

reason: Exact optimum area plus an attaining universal cover needs matching lower bound over all compact convex covers. Improving a geometric upper bound is not the requested result.
statement:
For a nonempty set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ let

$$
\operatorname{diam}(S) = \sup\{\, |x-y| : x, y \in S \,\},
$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm. Say that a set $C \subset
\mathbb{R}^2$ *covers* $S$ if there is an isometry
$\varphi$ of the plane (translations, rotations and reflections being allowed) with $\varphi(S)
\subseteq C$. Call a compact convex set $C \subset
\mathbb{R}^2$ a *universal cover* if $C$ covers every set
$S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $\operatorname{diam}(S) \le 1$, and put

$$
\alpha = \inf \{\, \operatorname{area}(C) : C \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \text{ a compact convex universal cover} \,\}.
$$

Determine the exact value of
$\alpha$, and exhibit a compact convex universal cover $C$ with
$\operatorname{area}(C) = \alpha$.
title: Lebesgue's universal covering problem

reason: Exact plane chromatic number requires matching infinite-plane coloring and obstruction. A finite unit-distance graph only supplies a lower bound unless it closes the gap.
statement:
For a set $S$, call a map $c:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to S$ a proper coloring of the plane
if

$$
c(x)\neq c(y)\quad\text{whenever } x,y\in\mathbb{R}^{2} \text{ satisfy } |x-y|=1,
$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm. Equivalently, let $G$ be the
unit-distance graph of the plane: the graph whose vertex set is
$\mathbb{R}^{2}$, with $xy$ an edge if and only if
$|x-y|=1$; a proper coloring of the plane is exactly a proper vertex coloring of $G$.

Determine the chromatic number of the plane,

$$
\chi(G)=\min\bigl\{\,k\in\mathbb{N} \;:\; \text{there exists a proper coloring } c:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\{1,\dots,k\}\,\bigr\},
$$

that is, the least number of colors with which the points of the plane can be
colored so that no two points at distance exactly $1$ receive the same color.
title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem

reason: General locally compact group actions on all manifold dimensions require topological exclusion beyond special dimensions/regularities. Do not exploit omitted conventional manifold qualifications as a discovery.
statement:
Let
$M$ be a topological manifold (a Hausdorff space, locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{n}$
for some $n \ge 0$), and let
$G$ be a locally compact topological group. Say that a continuous action $\Phi
\colon G \times M \to M$, written $\Phi(g,x) = g \cdot
x$, is *effective* (faithful) if its kernel is trivial, i.e. if $g \in
G$ satisfies $g \cdot x = x$ for every $x \in M$, then $g$ is the identity
element of $G$.

For every locally compact topological group
$G$ admitting a continuous effective action on a topological manifold $M$, the
group $G$ is a Lie group, i.e. $G$ carries a smooth manifold structure
compatible with its topology for which multiplication and inversion are smooth.

Equivalently: for every prime number $p$, the additive group $\mathbb{Z}_{p}$ of
$p$-adic integers, with its usual compact topology, admits no continuous
effective action on any topological manifold.
title: Hilbert–Smith conjecture

reason: Kadison-Singer has a classical published resolution warning; no MSS proof body read here. Formalizing/reconstructing that theorem is ineligible, registry and body clearance not claimed.
statement:
Let
$\ell^2$ denote the Hilbert space of square-summable sequences of complex numbers, with standard orthonormal basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$.
Let
$B$ be the C*-algebra of all bounded (continuous) linear operators from $\ell^2$
to $\ell^2$, and let $D\subseteq
B$ be the C*-subalgebra consisting of those operators that are diagonal with respect to $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$,
i.e. of those $T\in B$ for which there is a bounded sequence
$(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of complex numbers with $Te_n=\lambda_n
e_n$ for all $n$. Both $B$ and $D$ contain the identity operator $I$.

For a C*-algebra $A$ with multiplicative identity $I$, a *state* on
$A$ is a continuous linear functional $\varphi:A\to\mathbb{C}$ such that
$\varphi(I)=1$ and $\varphi(T)\geq 0$ for every positive $T\in
A$ (i.e. every $T$ of the form $T=S^*S$). The set of states on $A$ is convex,
and a state
$\varphi$ is called *pure* if it is an extreme point of this set, that is, if $\varphi=t\varphi_1+(1-t)\varphi_2$
with $0<t<1$ and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ states on
$A$ forces $\varphi_1=\varphi_2=\varphi$. A state $\psi$ on $B$ is said to
*extend* a state $\varphi$ on $D$ if $\psi(T)=\varphi(T)$ for all $T\in D$.

For every pure state $\varphi$ on $D$ there exists exactly one state
$\psi$ on $B$ that extends $\varphi$.
title: Kadison–Singer problem

reason: Fixed-degree limiting distribution requires concentration and total-mass tightness, not just expected degree asymptotics. Likely successor enumeration results must be body-mapped before a new target exists.
statement:
For each integer $k\geq 1$, let $Z^{(k)}_n$ denote the proportion of vertices of degree $k$ in a uniformly random planar graph with $n$ vertices. **Limiting degree-distribution conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, the random variable $Z^{(k)}_n$ converges in law to an explicit constant $\pi^{(k)}$, and these constants satisfy

$$
\sum_k\pi^{(k)}=1.
$$

This conjecture proposes a limiting probability distribution for vertex degrees in uniformly random planar graphs; the stated passage does not indicate that it has been resolved.
title: Conjecture on the limiting degree distribution of random planar graphs

reason: Explicitly excludes interval Julia sets, so source counterexample cannot refute modified scope. Need semigroup-wide Julia rigidity, not method similarity to the original counterexample.
statement:
Let $G$ be a polynomial semigroup, and write $J(G)$ for its Julia set. Suppose that there is an element $h\in G$ such that $J_h=J(G)$, and assume that $J(G)$ is not a line segment.

**Hinkkanen–Martin's modified conjecture.** For all $f,g\in G$, one has

$$
J_f=J_g.
$$

Consequently, $G$ is nearly abelian.

The original statement without the condition that $J(G)$ is not a line segment is refuted by a counterexample in the paper, whose Julia set is a closed line segment. The modified statement is explicitly described as unresolved.
title: Hinkkanen–Martin conjecture on Julia sets of polynomial semigroups

reason: Literal infinitude is stated equivalent to twin primes. Weight reparameterization supplies no tractable full-scope mechanism or independent discovery.
statement: Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime, and let its weight be the weight in the paper's decomposition of primes. The smallest member of each twin-prime pair other than $3$ has weight $3$. **Weight-three prime conjecture.** The number of primes with weight equal to $3$ is infinite. This is a reformulation of the twin prime conjecture in the terminology of the paper; no proof is known.
title: The infinitude of primes of weight 3

reason: Read v2 Sections1,6,8 and Theorem2.1 context. Literal record already restricts to classes of orderly currencies, so nonproper ++- from (1,3,4) is outside assigned scope and not a refutation. Finite coin check gives no proper-pattern obstruction. Source Proposition6.1 excludes one pattern and supplies selected normalized families, but no normalization preserving every proper sign pattern. No full constructive route or successor-body clearance; park.
statement:
Let a $+/-$-class be a class of orderly currencies determined by a specified $+/-$ pattern, and suppose that this class is non-empty. **Representative-with-first-coin-two conjecture.** The class has a representative currency

$$
A=(1,a_1,\ldots,a_k)
$$

with $a_1=2$. This conjecture concerns the existence of a particularly normalized representative for every non-empty $+/-$-class; the source reports that no counterexample was known, and it remains open.
title: Representative-with-first-coin-two conjecture for non-empty +/- classes

reason: All positive nu0 and real convolution times require positivity of a continuous mixture, not the disproved discrete half-integer version. No Mellin/Laplace positivity mechanism established.
title: Cufaro Petroni's non-integer convolution mixture conjecture

reason: Literal statement omits the differential equation entirely between display delimiters. Cannot assign meaningful global-solution quantifiers or assert a resolution from this record; primary reconstruction required.
statement:
Consider the differential equation

and its smooth global solutions. **Finiteness conjecture.** There are only finitely many smooth global solutions to

. This finiteness would justify the use of a numerical solver to determine the number of global solutions for a given M-shaped $\phi$, and the source leaves it as an open conjecture.
title: Finiteness conjecture for smooth global solutions

reason: All symplectic manifolds and spectral-bounded symplectomorphisms require general unboundedness obstruction. Hofer analogue and special manifolds do not establish the spectral statement.
statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold, let $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$ be its identity component, and let $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ be the Hamiltonian subgroup. Let $\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega,\gamma)$ denote the subgroup of symplectomorphisms bounded with respect to the spectral norm $\gamma$. **Spectral bounded isometry conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega,\gamma)=\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)\qquad\text{for all }(M,\omega).
$$

This is the spectral-norm analogue of the bounded isometry conjecture for the Hofer norm. The source formulates it as a conjecture after noting that the Hofer version is very hard and that partial results are known.
title: Spectral bounded isometry conjecture

reason: Read v1 definitions, Section4 Theorem6 and Corollary7 proof, concluding conjecture. Source upper bound excludes points only above e log n+alpha; d(212)+1 already defeats that sufficient filter. Pell/Pisot rounding decay does not extend to e. No all-depth membership invariant; no further sweep warranted.
statement:
Let $w(i,j)=j/i$ be the weight function, and let $\mathcal{A}_\infty=\{1,3,8,22,60,\ldots\}$. Let $d(0)=1$ and, for $n\geq 1$, define

$$
d(n)=\lfloor e d(n-1)+0.5\rfloor.
$$

Thus the sequence begins $1,3,8,22,60,163,443,\ldots$.

**Jumping-sequence characterization.** The set $\mathcal{A}_\infty$ is composed of the elements of the integer sequence $d(n)$.

The preceding results show that the sequence elements can belong to $\mathcal{A}_\infty$ and provide an upper bound excluding sufficiently large integers outside the sequence, but the paper notes that the available rounding estimates do not establish this characterization.
title: The jumping-sequence characterization of the infinite admissible set

reason: Matrices A,B and identity eq.further.1 are not defined literally. Odd-dimensional skew symmetry alone does not prove noncommutative determinant correction with q_i=(n-i)h1. Need actual algebra and ordered-product identity first.
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $A$ and $B$ be the matrices occurring in the identity $\operatorname{eq.further.1}$, with parameters $h_1$ and $q_i$. A matrix is **antisymmetric** when it is equal to the negative of its transpose. **Odd-dimensional antisymmetric-solution conjecture.** If $n$ is odd and at least one of $A$ and $B$ is antisymmetric, then $\operatorname{eq.further.1}$ holds with

$$
q_i=(n-i)h_1.
$$

This generalizes the antisymmetric solution observed for $n=3$ and $n=5$, but the paper does not establish it for all odd $n$.
title: Odd-dimensional antisymmetric solution conjecture for noncommutative determinants

reason: Record explicitly reports source five-dimensional counterexample. Reconstructing that example is ineligible; reported refutation not independently proof-body verified here.
statement:
Let $P$ be a reflexive polytope with barycenter $b_P=0$. For a facet $F$ of $P$, let a facet $G$ be adjacent to $F$ when there is a vector $u_G$ such that

$$
\langle u_G,G\rangle=-1,\qquad \langle u_G,P\rangle\geq -1.
$$

**Chan–Leung's facet-point conjecture.** If $b_P=0$, then for every facet $F$ there exists a point $x_F\in\operatorname{aff}(F)$ such that

$$
\langle u_G,x_F\rangle\leq\frac12
$$

for every facet $G$ of $P$ adjacent to $F$.

The conjecture was proposed as a combinatorial ingredient for proving the Chan–Leung Chern-number inequality without additional assumptions. The source gives a five-dimensional counterexample, so the assertion is refuted.
title: Chan–Leung's facet-point conjecture for reflexive polytopes

reason: Formal identity requires exact partition function and all-degree symmetric-function control. Macdonald/Hilbert-scheme results are possible subsumers, but no exact body bridge checked; finite coefficients cannot settle it.
statement:
Let $\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)$ be the partition function appearing in the source, let $\phi(0):=0$, and for every nonzero partition $\lambda$ define

$$
\phi_\lambda(z,w):=\sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}z^{j-1}w^{i-1},
$$

where the sum is over the boxes of $\lambda$. **Hilbert-scheme identity.** The following formal power-series identity is conjectured:

$$
1+(z^2-1)(1-w^2)\frac{\sum_\lambda\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)\phi_\lambda(z^2,w^2)T^{|\lambda|}}{\sum_\lambda\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)T^{|\lambda|}}=\prod_{n\geq1}\frac{(1-zwT^n)^2}{(1-z^2T^n)(1-w^2T^n)}.
$$

It arises by combining the Hilbert-scheme formula with the main conjecture in the case $g=1$ and $\mu=(n-1,1)$, giving a purely combinatorial reformulation.
title: Hilbert-scheme identity for character varieties

reason: Read v1 recurrence(3),(12), Proposition4 proof, Proposition5 statement/selected induction and Conjecture6. Unfolding yields quadratic branching, not a single sequence. Exact six-level c1=c2=1 check confirms rational roots/residuals only. Products of Somos terms are not closed under taking reduced numerator divisors automatically; no factor-closure invariant or all-parameter route established.
statement: Let $T$ be the recurrence tree generated by the recurrence referred to as (Som4Ord3), and let the generalized Somos-4 sequence be the sequence associated with that recurrence. **Product structure conjecture.** Every integer in $T$, and the numerator and denominator of every reduced non-integer rational number in $T$, are products of terms in the generalized Somos-4 sequence. The observation is motivated by the unexpectedly simple polynomial sequence found in the recurrence tree, whereas the closed form for the generalised Somos-4 sequence is expressed using elliptic theta functions. The source presents this broader product property as something observed rather than proved.
title: Product structure conjecture for the generalized Somos-4 recurrence tree

reason: Almost-sure sublinear capacity for arbitrary transient walks needs tail-robust growth argument. Stable-law examples or finite aggregates do not imply the universal claim.
statement:
Let $R$ be a transient random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $A_n$ be the aggregate after $n$ particles. Write $\operatorname{Cap}(A_n)$ for its capacity. **Capacity sparsity conjecture.** Almost surely,

$$
\operatorname{Cap}(A_n)=o(n).
$$

The conjecture concerns the capacity growth of aggregates generated by arbitrary transient random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$. The surrounding discussion gives no proof or counterexample, so its status remains open.
title: Capacity sparsity conjecture for transient random-walk aggregation

reason: All-degree braided symmetrizers and domains are only implicitly specified. Low-degree projector calculations leave the asserted general operator identity and existence hypotheses unresolved.
statement:
Let ${\rm Tr}_R L^k\in {\cal L}^k(R)$ be the braided trace power, and let $P_+^{(k)}$ and $P_{+2}^{(k-1)}$ be the symmetrizer operators acting on the corresponding tensor powers. **Projector relation.** For every positive integer $k$ for which these operators are defined, the relation

$$
P_+^{(k)}{\rm Tr}_R L^k=P_{+2}^{(k-1)}{\rm Tr}_R L^k
$$

holds. This identity is used to put the homogeneous element ${\rm Tr}_R L^k$ into the canonical form required before applying the differential in the complex of braided differential forms. The source presents the relation without resolving its general status; the preceding discussion indicates that explicit projector constructions are known only in low degrees.
title: The projector relation for braided trace powers

reason: Quotient by easily described and lower-K identities is not literally defined. Need exact vector spaces/relations and rank formula for every K; finite nullspace computations alone are insufficient.
statement:
Let a subgraph-counting identity be an identity of the form described above, involving induced-subgraph counts in the neighborhoods and non-neighborhoods of vertices, and classify identities by quotienting out the easily described families and the difficult identities for lower values of $K$.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** For every $K\geq4$, there is only one subgraph-counting identity modulo the easily described families and the difficult identities for lower $K$.

This conjecture asserts uniqueness at each complexity level after the stated equivalences are imposed. The paper does not provide a proof or resolution of this claim.
title: Uniqueness of difficult subgraph-counting identities

reason: Arbitrary pseudodifferential operator bundles require global reduction or residue-characteristic-class obstruction. The identity-symbol subgroup theorem does not automatically extend to full structure group.
statement: Let $\Psi{\rm DO}_0^*$ be the group of invertible zeroth-order classical pseudodifferential operators, and let $\mathcal E$ be a $\Psi{\rm DO}_0^*$-bundle over a base manifold admitting a partition of unity. The Wodzicki-Chern classes $c_k^{\rm w}(\mathcal E)$ are defined using the Wodzicki residue applied to powers of the curvature. **Wodzicki-Chern vanishing conjecture.** The Wodzicki-Chern classes vanish on any $\Psi{\rm DO}_0^*$-bundle over a base manifold admitting a partition of unity. The preceding theorem proves vanishing when the structure group reduces to the subgroup of operators with identity leading symbol; the conjecture asserts the corresponding statement for arbitrary invertible zeroth-order pseudodifferential-operator bundles.
title: The vanishing conjecture for Wodzicki-Chern classes of pseudodifferential operator bundles

reason: Group von Neumann algebra embedding requires precise hyperlinear-group connection; general Connes-embedding refutation cannot simply be asserted to settle this restricted group scope without a bridge. Current registry unavailable.
statement: Let $G$ be a countable i.c.c. group, meaning that every conjugacy class other than the identity class is infinite, and let $VN(G)$ be its group von Neumann algebra. Let $R$ be the hyperfinite type $II_1$ factor and let $R^{\omega}$ denote a suitable ultrapower of $R$. **Connes' embedding conjecture for groups.** For every countable i.c.c. group $G$, the group von Neumann algebra $VN(G)$ embeds into a suitable ultrapower $R^{\omega}$. This is presented as a weaker algebraic version of Connes' embedding conjecture, with the source giving no resolution.
title: Connes' embedding conjecture for groups

reason: All non-even p and three signed terms need explicit frequency/sign family and analytic norm gap over intervals. Known majorant counterexamples with more terms do not settle the three-term requirement; precise p domain and successors uninspected.
statement: Let $\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ be the one-dimensional torus, and write $e_k(x):=e^{2\pi i kx}$. An idempotent polynomial is an exponential sum with coefficients in $\{0,1\}$; a three-term idempotent counterexample is a signed version whose $p$-norm exceeds that of the corresponding all-positive idempotent polynomial. **Three-term idempotent counterexample conjecture.** For every $p$ that is not an even integer, there are three-term idempotent counterexamples in the Hardy–Littlewood majorant problem. The conjecture asserts the existence of such counterexamples, while the source does not state a resolution here.
title: Three-term idempotent counterexample conjecture

reason: Average bounded-cell diameter across all simple arrangements needs global combinatorial charging or scalable violation. Individual high-diameter cells do not refute the average conjecture; no full route identified.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a simple arrangement of $n$ hyperplanes in dimension $d$, and let $H_\mathcal{A}(n,d)$ be the maximum average graph diameter of its bounded cells.

**Hyperplane Diameter Conjecture.**

$$
H_\mathcal{A}(n,d) \leq d.
$$

The conjecture concerns the average diameter of bounded cells in simple hyperplane arrangements. The supplied material gives no resolution status.
title: Hyperplane Diameter Conjecture for bounded cells of arrangements
